Phase 63 plan: docs/phases/roadmap-placeholders-are-not-phases.md @ 37189f2 (branch phase/roadmap-placeholders-are-not-phases). The arbiter approved opening this cycle and is away; he asked me to continue through the handoff.

Defect: the roadmap tagteam setup seeds fails tagteam roadmap check on 3.14.1 — 'duplicate slug name: Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3' and 'name: depends on itself' — because the three '### Phase N: [Name]' headings slugify identically. Reproduced in an empty directory. 9 of 41 registered projects still carry the unedited seed and are refused by roadmap ready/queue/graph and full-roadmap mode.

Plan: a heading whose whole title is one bracketed token is a placeholder, not a phase — skipped by parse_roadmap() (sections still split on every heading) and validate_identities(), reported via Phase 60's warn channel; a placeholder-only roadmap is 'ok: 0 phase(s)' for check, while parse_roadmap() keeps raising ValueError when there is no real phase (launch.py / watcher.py / worktree.py catch that today; an empty list would be a new shape). I rejected distinct placeholder titles: check would pass but roadmap ready would offer 'first-phase-name' as startable, and it fixes no existing project.

Coupling I want checked: SEED_FILES reads data/templates/roadmap.md, which since Phases 61/62 is also the byte-for-byte provenance that lets a project's templates/roadmap.md be retired. Editing the seed in place would silently turn other users' not-yet-upgraded copies into 'custom'. So seeds move to data/seeds/, data/templates + data/checklists are frozen and pinned to git show v3.14.1 by a test, and only the seed copy gets its dead commands (/phase, /plan create, /status) replaced. The shipped-docs audit learns that family, with the frozen directory excluded explicitly.

Please press on: (1) the placeholder rule ^\[[^\]]*\]$ on the whole title — too narrow / too wide; (2) exit 0 + 'ok: 0 phase(s)' for a placeholder-only roadmap vs the unchanged ValueError elsewhere; (3) whether freezing data/checklists too is right given bench falls back to it; (4) a real phase depending on a placeholder staying 'unknown dependency'.

Verified: tagteam roadmap check ok (64 phases). No code changed; suite not run (plan cycle).

The direction is sound: whole-title bracket placeholders should not become runnable phases, retaining all strict headings as section boundaries avoids metadata bleed, and separating mutable seeds from frozen retirement evidence fixes the provenance coupling. Unknown dependencies on omitted placeholders are appropriate. Freezing the checklist sources is reasonable for this scope; bench can be decoupled when its content actually needs to evolve.

Please revise two concrete gaps before implementation:

1. The planned check fallback (ValueError + placeholders + no non-placeholder strict heading -> success) can suppress identity errors. Example:
   ### Phase 1: [Name]
   ### Phase 2:
   validate_identities() correctly reports Phase 2: empty name, but graph_problems() computes that list before parse_roadmap(), whose new no-real-phase ValueError prevents returning it. The proposed fallback then prints ok: 0 phase(s) and exits 0. Require that identity validation has no problems before accepting the placeholder-only case, and preserve/report those problems otherwise. Add a regression for a placeholder plus a bare empty-name heading (and duplicate empty-name headings if useful); check must exit 1, while the untouched seed exits 0. Do not broadly turn unrelated ValueErrors into placeholder success.

2. The proposed old-command audit exemption covers data/templates/ only, but tagteam/data/history/v3.3.0/templates/roadmap.md:37-39 also contains /phase, /plan create and /status. Those historical bytes are frozen and used for reconstructible retirement, so the new audit would bounce this plan as written. Specify a narrow, explicit provenance exemption for the older-command audit that also covers that historical source, with tag/hash pinning maintained. Keep the existing /handoff-* audit policy intact unless a change to it is explicitly justified. Do not edit the frozen historical roadmap or silently lose its recovery bytes.

Review based on roadmap.py parse/identity/check control flow and a read-only search of shipped Markdown. No code changed; no test suite run.

Plan round 2 @ 82cc689 — both findings accepted; changes in Scope 2 and 5, Technical Approach, Success Criteria 7 and 12.

1. Masking. Confirmed from graph_problems(): identities are computed, then parse_roadmap()'s ValueError discards them, so my exception-based fallback would have printed ok for '[Name]' + bare '### Phase 2:'. The placeholder-only success is now decided on positive evidence, never by an except: check calls validate_identities() itself first; new placeholder_only(text) = >=1 placeholder and no lenient-pattern heading that is not a placeholder. placeholder_only + identity problems -> 'roadmap invalid', exit 1, problems listed; placeholder_only + none -> 'ok: 0 phase(s)', exit 0, without calling graph_problems(). Otherwise the existing path runs unchanged, including how it reports every other ValueError. Criterion 7: placeholder + bare heading -> exit 1 with 'Phase 2: empty name'; placeholder + two bare '### Phase 2:' -> empty-name and duplicate-number; untouched seed -> exit 0.

2. Audit exemption. Confirmed by search: exactly two shipped .md files carry the older family — tagteam/data/templates/roadmap.md and tagteam/data/history/v3.3.0/templates/roadmap.md — both frozen provenance, neither edited. The exemption is an allowlist of those two exact paths (no directory, no pattern); the test asserts each allowlisted path is covered by a tag-pin test (history by Phase 62's table test, data/templates by this phase's freeze test) and that a temp .md outside the allowlist fails the same scan. The /handoff-* audit is untouched and keeps scanning both files. Criterion 12.

No code changed; suite not run (plan cycle).

The two-path, tag-pinned exemption resolves the audit finding. One small control-flow correction remains in the written plan before approval.

Scope item 2 now correctly says check runs validate_identities first and reports its problems. However Technical Approach says to run/report that validation only WHEN placeholder_only(text) holds, otherwise use the existing path unchanged. Those are different algorithms. For the required regression '[Name]' + bare '### Phase 2:', placeholder_only is false because the lenient pattern sees the non-placeholder empty name. The existing graph_problems path then loses its identity list when parse_roadmap raises, so check exits 1 with the generic no-real-phases message instead of listing 'Phase 2: empty name' (and duplicate-number problems in the second fixture). Thus Success Criterion 7 is still not achieved by the Technical Approach.

Make the technical steps agree with Scope and the acceptance tests: preserve and report identity problems independently of the placeholder_only success branch. For example, in the no-real-phase case evaluate/report validate_identities before allowing placeholder-only success; otherwise retain existing graph validation/aggregation. Keep arbitrary ValueError handling as failure. This is a plan-text correction, not a request to broaden scope or change the placeholder rule.

No other blockers found. Plan review only; no tests run or implementation files changed.
